decisive_budget.rule: A0 relational coverage on DEV at 1,024 = 50.0%, below 90%

prompts.reader: Answer the question using only the memory below. If the memory does not contain the answer, reply exactly: Not in memory. Use at most 15 words.
prompts.judge: Question, reference answer, response. Does the response give the same answer as the reference (wording, extra detail and date format may differ)? Reply CORRECT or WRONG.

harness_notes: Shared rare words: a word in one turn cannot be shared, so the vocabulary whose rarest 5% counts is the words found in two or more turns.
Discovery drops a resolution whose partition is identical to one already kept: it would only add an identical step to the walk.
Filling a packet, a turn that does not fit the remaining budget is skipped and the next one is tried.
Adversarial replies are parsed by trimming whitespace and a final period and ignoring case before comparing with 'Not in memory'.
Evidence ids are split on ';', ',' and spaces; a question naming an id that is not a turn is left out of stage 1.
The write path refuses turns that are only a question; they are missing for every arm (DEV: 2 of 419 and 20 of 689 turns; one DEV open-domain question lost its evidence that way).
When forgetting, a turn whose stored record was shared with a forgotten turn counts as forgotten too.

Observed on DEV, not changed: A2's attach threshold is the 25th percentile of member-to-own-centroid similarity, and members helped form their centroid, so most later turns stay loose in the frozen arm (conv-26: 145 of 164).
Observed on DEV, not changed: the judge is lenient with partial answers; the human audit (gate) checks it.

The first full DEV stage 2 (started 06:09 on 2026-11-20) hung after the laptop suspended on battery at 07:28 and was stopped with no output. Stage 2 now saves each answered row and resumes; a hung call is retried. Calls are deterministic, so neither changes what is measured.

Stage 2 asks the reader for every row of a conversation before the judge grades any. Alternating them made Ollama reload the 27B reader after each judge call (DEV, 2026-11-20: about 37 s per reader call instead of 10 s). Calls are deterministic and the judge never sees the arm, so the order changes nothing measured. DEV stage 2 rows answered before this change were judged one at a time.

Added after DEV, outside the gates as written (the four forgetting checks are unchanged): forgetting also rewrites A3's saved versions and removes forgotten turn ids from its revision log, so a rollback cannot bring a forgotten turn back; stage 1 reports what is left there (history_passed).

Added after DEV, outside the gates: each packet records its time, groups visited and member similarities read, since equal tokens are not equal work; stage 1 also times each arm's build. The protocol's full packet trace (version, nodes visited with scores, each turn's route) is written for every question and arm at the decisive budget to <out>.traces.jsonl, whose hash goes into the stage 1 output. DEV stage 1 was rerun with these additions on 2026-11-20: all 16,212 coverage cells, the summary and the scope checks are identical to the first run, which is kept in artifacts/m1/superseded/. Without the version rewrite, every saved A3 version on DEV (8 of 8 and 13 of 13) still listed forgotten turns.

Scope isolation checks the project filter (_is_about) inside one owner's store. It is not an authorization boundary or a multi-user security test; the remote service separates owners into distinct encrypted stores.

No LoCoMo turn reaches the 2,000-character write limit (longest: 454 characters across all 10 conversations, a length count only). Turns are lost only to the filter for turns that are only a question (see above); stage 1 reports every refused turn with its reason and the questions whose evidence is missing from the store, which bound every arm's coverage alike.
